result: Primary human airway epithelial cells express multiple SLC4A family members at mRNA level, with SLC4A4 being the most highly expressed, followed by SLC4A7, SLC4A8, and SLC4A5. Isoforms B/C of SLC4A4 (NBCe1) were more highly expressed than isoform A. Bestrophins were also expressed but at 1-2 logs lower levels than the major SLC4A transporters.
evaluation: Reviewers raised concerns about the relative expression assessment, questioning how mRNA abundance was determined and whether PCR bands were validated by digestion (Reviewer 3). They also specifically requested information about Bestrophin expression (Reviewers 1 and 2), which the authors addressed but reviewers questioned the interpretation of relative expression levels, particularly for SLC4A7 which 'looks as if the expression could be quite reasonable' despite authors claiming low expression.

result: S0859 inhibits basal HCO3- secretion in primary human airway epithelial cells under unstimulated conditions, with no effect on short-circuit current in the absence of HCO3-. Interestingly, S0859 did not reduce forskolin-stimulated HCO3- secretion under the tested conditions. The results suggest an electrogenic HCO3- transporter at the basolateral membrane consistent with SLC4A4, as SLC4A7 and SLC4A8 are electroneutral and SLC4A5 localizes apically in other tissues.
evaluation: Reviewers raised significant concerns about these findings. Reviewer 2 noted the S0859-inhibitable current is 'very small (~1 uAmp/cm2) in comparison with anion current measurements in similar cell models reported previously (~20 uAmp/cm2)' and questioned the quality of the monolayers. Reviewers 1 and 2 challenged the logic for excluding SLC4A5 and SLC4A8, stating the arguments are 'weak' because electrogenic transport doesn't prove the importer is electrogenic, and localization in other tissues doesn't rule out different localization in airways. They also questioned S0859 selectivity for SLC4A4 versus other family members.

result: Intracellular pH recovery experiments show that exposing cells to CO2/HCO3- induces acidification that recovers in a Na+-dependent manner when basolateral HCO3- is present. S0859 blocks this pHi recovery from CO2-induced acidification, even in the presence of NHE inhibitor DMA, demonstrating SLC4A4-dependent bicarbonate uptake.
evaluation: Reviewers did not raise specific concerns about these intracellular pH recovery experiments. The data clearly demonstrate Na+-dependent, S0859-sensitive bicarbonate uptake at the basolateral membrane, supporting the role of SLC4A4 in intracellular pH regulation.

result: SLC4A4 inhibition with S0859 significantly decreased ASL pH under resting conditions (t1/2 = 46 min) and partially prevented forskolin-induced increases in ASL pH (increasing half-time from 25 to 31 min). When S0859 was added after forskolin, it reduced the CFTR-dependent ASL pH increase with a half-time of 14 min, confirming SLC4A4's central role in ASL pH homeostasis.
evaluation: Reviewers requested clarification about the timing of pH measurements and the difference in timescales between intracellular acidification effects (Figure 1) versus ASL pH effects which 'seems to take ~2hrs' (Reviewer 3). They also asked for methods details about when pH was considered settled and what the data points represent in the summary figures. The slower timescale for ASL pH changes compared to intracellular effects was not adequately explained.

result: Immunolocalization studies show SLC4A4 protein is expressed in the basolateral membrane of acetylated tubulin-positive cells, indicating preferential expression in ciliated cells in human airways.
evaluation: Reviewers raised significant concerns about cell type localization. Reviewer 2 noted that 'it is unclear how many other cell types (CC10-positive Club cells; ionocytes; goblet cells) are retrieved in these human airway cell cultures' and that in mouse airways and previous studies, 'CFTR (and pendrin) are expressed mainly in CC10+-secretory (Club) cells, not in ciliated cells.' This raises the question whether SLC4A4 is also expressed in human Club cells and whether Club cells rather than ciliated cells are the major sources of HCO3- secretion. Reviewers suggested immunostaining for CC10+ cells to clarify this issue.

result: Mouse airway epithelium expresses multiple SLC4 family members including Slc4a4 (isoform B/C but not A), Slc4a5, Slc4a7, and Slc4a10. In Ussing chamber experiments, UTP-induced anion current was significantly reduced in the absence of HCO3-, but cAMP-induced anion secretion and amiloride-sensitive sodium absorption were unaffected. Acetazolamide had no effect on UTP-induced current, indicating de novo HCO3- synthesis does not participate.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 questioned why 'the IBMX/forskolin/cAMP-induced anion current, in contrast to the UTP/ca2+-induced current, is not reduced in bicarbonate-free buffer, i.e. does not seem to have a HCO3- component' noting that 'in mouse trachea, most if not all Fsk/cAMP-induced anion secretory current is CaCC-mediated, so there is a priori no reason why forskolin-induced currents would not be reduced (at least in part) in a HCO3- free buffer.' This discrepancy was not adequately explained.

result: S0859 inhibited cAMP-induced anion current in mouse trachea, but when TMEM16A/CFTR were blocked with CaCCinhA01, S0859 still reduced current, indicating that electrogenic bicarbonate secretion was not significantly stimulated by cAMP. Basal HCO3- secretion occurs in mouse trachea, as S0859 reduced basal current only in HCO3- buffer. UTP-induced anion secretion was significantly reduced by S0859 in HCO3- buffer but not in HEPES buffer.
evaluation: Reviewers raised concerns about the interpretation of these experiments. Reviewer 2 asked 'how do the authors explain that subsequent addition of S0859 further inhibits a "basal" HCO3- secretory current? Does HCO3- exit the cell at the apical side through tonically active CFTR, or through an electrogenic HCO3-/Cl- exchanger (but pendrin is electroneutral)?' The mechanism of basal bicarbonate secretion and the apical exit pathway remain unclear. Reviewer 3 also questioned whether Isc measurements truly represent 'resting conditions' given that 'the ASL is essentially flooded and the ionic composition on the apical side is not likely to match that of a normal ASL.'

result: UTP induced intracellular acidification in murine airway cells that was significantly reduced in low Cl- buffer (indicating Cl-/HCO3- exchange) and nearly absent in HEPES buffer without HCO3-. S0859 induced acidification and prevented UTP-induced acidification, with partial restoration after washout, suggesting both basal and UTP-induced HCO3- secretion depend on SLC4A4 activity.
evaluation: Reviewers noted that 'some effects are not fully reversible (Figure S3G)' and requested comment on this observation (Reviewer 3). The incomplete reversibility raises questions about potential off-target effects or irreversible changes. Additionally, Reviewers 1 and 2 noted the 'transient negative change in Isc elicited by S0859' and asked whether 'the compound has transient off-target effects on the intracellular ca2+ level, or activates basolateral K+ channels,' noting it is 'remarkable that similar deflections are not seen in human AECs.'

result: Slc4a4-/- mice showed defects in tracheal cartilage formation with ventral gaps and abnormal patterns. SLC4A4 signal was nearly absent in knockout airways. In mouse, SLC4A4 was preferentially expressed in CCSP-positive Club cells and excluded from ciliated cells, with this pattern maintained in distal airways. Knockout mice demonstrated adherent mucus at the epithelial surface and signs of damaged epithelium with interruptions in the epithelial layer, which prevented electrophysiological measurements due to decreased transepithelial resistance.
evaluation: Reviewers did not raise specific concerns about these histological and immunolocalization findings in the knockout mice. The data clearly demonstrate the lung phenotype and the differential cell-type expression pattern between mouse (Club cells) and human (ciliated cells) airways, which the authors acknowledge and discuss.

result: Slc4a4-/- cells showed decreased magnitude of intracellular acidification during UTP stimulation compared to wild type, suggesting an important amount of HCO3- accumulates in airway cells via SLC4A4. After UTP washout, acidification persisted in wild type but not knockout cells, suggesting HCO3- secretion was sustained by SLC4A4 activity.
evaluation: Reviewers did not raise specific concerns about these intracellular pH measurements in knockout versus wild type cells. The data support the role of SLC4A4 in bicarbonate accumulation and sustained secretion.

result: Mucociliary clearance measurements showed plastic beads covered larger distances in wild type compared to Slc4a4-/- tracheas, with retrograde movement observed in knockouts. Wild type tissues in HEPES buffer showed similar reduction in distance traveled as knockouts, but HEPES buffer had no further effect in knockout tracheas, demonstrating that mucociliary clearance is significantly decreased when HCO3- transport is impaired.
evaluation: While reviewers did not directly challenge the mucociliary clearance data, Reviewer 3 noted that 'direct measurements of ASL volume and pH in the knockout mice would clearly strengthen part of the central thesis, although these measurements are admittedly difficult to perform.' The authors acknowledge they could not measure ASL pH in mouse trachea due to 'technically challenging issues.' Reviewer 3 also asked 'is there any evidence of changes to mucus rheology in the hAEC cultures accompanying the changes in pH?' which was not addressed.

result: Slc4a4-null mice revealed a previously unreported lung phenotype characterized by mucus accumulation and reduced mucociliary clearance. The reduction of SLC4A4 function induced a CF-like phenotype even when chloride secretion remained intact, highlighting SLC4A4's important role in bicarbonate secretion and mammalian airway function.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this as a key finding of the paper. The public review states the paper 'identifies the sodium-bicarbonate cotransporter SLC4A4 as a key component of the mechanism by which normal airways prevent the formation of sticky mucus.' While reviewers raised questions about specific mechanisms and measurements, they did not challenge the overall conclusion that loss of SLC4A4 produces a CF-like phenotype.

result: Slc4a4-null mice are affected by severe metabolic acidosis due to proximal renal tubular acidosis, with decreased plasma HCO3- (5.3±0.5 mM). However, it is unlikely that reduced HCO3- availability influenced mucus accumulation in the airways, as the transporter is fully saturated at 3 mM HCO3-.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 specifically questioned this interpretation, stating 'Whether the reduced level of plasma HCO3- contributes to the lack of HCO3- secretion and reduced ASL pH in the trachea of the Slc4a4-/- mouse depends on the affinity of the NBCe1 transporter for HCO3- ions. Therefore it is of interest to learn whether the transporter is already saturated at 5 mM HCO3-, or needs higher serosal HCO3- levels, e.g. 24 mM. This could be addressed experimentally or at least discussed.' The authors cite previous work showing saturation at 3 mM, but reviewers wanted this addressed more directly in the context of the systemic acidosis.

result: Both Slc4a4-/- and W516X-mutant animals die soon after weaning, while the specific knockout for isoform A (NBCe1-A) has normal lifespan but the knockout for isoforms B/C (NBCe1-B/C) is lethal. This suggests the cause of death is not due to metabolic acidosis but rather extra-renal phenotypes worsened by pRTA. Lethality is dependent on genetic background, supporting the influence of modifier genes.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge these observations about the mouse model phenotypes and lethality. The discussion of isoform-specific effects and genetic background influence was accepted as part of the characterization of the model.
